words.prose: {{ar:كٓهيعٓصٓ}} ({{tr:kāf hāʾ yāʾ ʿayn ṣād}}) is a whole ayah made from five recited letter-names, fused into one written token and carrying no ordinary lexical root. The QAC-compatible evidence lets the opener fill a predicate-like slot, so the bare sound-string is not merely a loose title; grammar quietly supplies a recoverable demonstrative frame while the audible field remains only the letters. The extended {{ar:كهيعص ذِكْرُ}} ({{tr:kāf hāʾ yāʾ ʿayn ṣād dhikru}}) reading and the next ayah's {{ar:ذِكْرُ رَحْمَتِ رَبِّكَ}} ({{tr:dhikru raḥmati rabbika}}) (19:2) expose the same pressure from another angle: the opener can stand as a complete recited sign, yet it leans forward into named remembrance before the Zakariyyā narrative begins. Its semantic force stays polyvalent. The reader is asked to hear alphabetic letter-names and an undecoded cipher at once; dhikr-framing, attention, oath-like or mnemonic possibilities, and controlled opacity remain live because no governor, root, or argument frame selects one normal dictionary sense. More speculative initial readings also remain as narrowed apparatus: speech-pressure from {{ar:ك}} ({{tr:kāf}}) as an initial of {{ar:كَلَام}} ({{tr:kalām}}), eye/spring/source/essence pressure around {{ar:ع}} ({{tr:ʿayn}}), divine-attribute initials such as generous, guiding, certainty-or-hand, knowing, and truthful, and prophetic-name initials that foreground the surrounding surah's John and Jesus narrative field can hover around the sequence, but they do not replace the local letter-recitation surface. Form and recitation do much of the work. The script marks selected letters for extended performance, makes five names into one orthographic word, and contrasts continuous delivery with a waqf form that individuates the same five recitation atoms into a measured cadence chain. Vowel-color variants, especially imāla tilting {{ar:ه}} ({{tr:hāʾ}}) and {{ar:ي}} ({{tr:yāʾ}}), the expanded {{ar:كافُ}} ({{tr:kāfu}}) form, and special notation around {{ar:ع}} ({{tr:ʿayn}}) show that the opener attracted recitational handling without becoming a derived word; {{ar:ي}} ({{tr:yāʾ}}) also remains a consonant and vowel-carrier pressure point. In the extended dhikr reading, final {{ar:ص}} ({{tr:ṣād}}) can even press into {{ar:ذِكْرُ}} ({{tr:dhikru}}), making the boundary itself audible. Sound is therefore not decoration: the sequence moves through velar, laryngeal, palatal, pharyngeal, and emphatic zones, so the reciter physically traverses a wide Arabic articulatory range before any narrative clause appears. Distribution sharpens the effect. This is the only five-letter muqattaʿāt sequence and the exact string is corpus-unique, while its final {{ar:ص}} ({{tr:ṣād}}) also has an independent opener identity in Surah 38 (38:1). The convergent payoff is that Surah 19 begins with a compact, rootless, qirāʾāt-sensitive, acoustically broad, and forward-leaning sign whose controlled opacity becomes the threshold into mercy-mention.

topics.headline: predicate-like letters lean toward dhikr completion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the bare letters can stand as a compressed nominal assertion while the dhikr reading and 19:2 reveal the same pressure toward explicit remembrance.
topics.reason: The aligned QAC row marks the token as PRED while also treating it as particle-like disconnected letters; the dhikr completion is therefore retained as variant and forward-bridge pressure, not as the canonical surface replacing the bare opener.

topics.headline: letter-names and cipher stay simultaneously live
topics.reader_payoff: The reader holds the opener as pronounced alphabet and unresolved sign at the same time, rather than collapsing it into one hidden paraphrase.
topics.reason: With no local governor, argument frame, or lexical root, the CRITICAL rows about alphabetic recitation, cipher status, attention, and dhikr-framing remain coherent without one function controlling the parse.

topics.headline: initial readings hover without decoding the opener
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees why attribute-initial, prophetic-initial, and letter-field readings can add pressure while the local word still remains five recited letters.
topics.reason: The supplied initial and acrostic proposals are preserved as interpretive apparatus, but the guardrail evidence gives no selected lexical decoding that would replace the local letter-name surface.

topics.headline: five letter-names become one ayah-word
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees language-material itself made into the whole ayah: five named letters are written as one rootless predicate-bearing token.
topics.reason: The aligned word has no root or form tag and is one orthographic unit, supporting the CRITICAL claims about fusion, marked recitation, and the shift away from derivational analysis.

topics.headline: variant vocalization colors the same sequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears that the same letter sequence can receive different vowel color and letter-name handling while preserving its identity.
topics.reason: The vowel and letter-name rows are meaningful qirāʾāt/form evidence, but they color or expand the recited token rather than replacing the canonical fused sequence.

topics.headline: continuous unit can be heard as five pause-units
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that continuity is itself a formal choice, because waqf evidence can re-expose the fused opener as five discrete recitation atoms.
topics.reason: The canonical local item is one continuous orthographic unit, so the pause-individuated form survives as contrastive recitational evidence rather than the controlling local delivery.

topics.headline: final sound can fuse into dhikr
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears how the extended dhikr reading can turn adjacency into a sound event when final {{ar:ص}} ({{tr:ṣād}}) presses into {{ar:ذِكْرُ}} ({{tr:dhikru}}).
topics.reason: Assimilation belongs to the extended reading with {{ar:ذِكْرُ}} ({{tr:dhikru}}), so it is retained as boundary pressure and not imposed on the canonical bare ayah.

topics.headline: the opener traverses the vocal tract
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah is experienced physically as a passage through contrasting articulation zones before it becomes a narratable proposition.
topics.reason: The five named letters supply velar, laryngeal, palatal, pharyngeal, and emphatic-dental textures; the phonetic rows describe that local sequence rather than importing outside lexical meaning.

topics.headline: the only five-letter muqattaʿāt token
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opener's length and exact form are not routine; this one-word ayah carries a corpus-unique five-letter sequence.
topics.reason: The QAC row explicitly notes the five-letter sequence as the longest muqattaʿāt, and the CRITICAL hapax rows supply the exact-token uniqueness claim.

topics.headline: letter-recitation becomes the surah threshold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader enters Surah 19 through recited phonemic material rather than narrative, command, praise, or an ordinary lexical sentence.
topics.reason: The whole ayah is a single rootless letter-name unit, so the CRITICAL rows about opening genre and clause-like phonological architecture are locally supported.

topics.headline: final ṣād has opener identity elsewhere
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final {{ar:ص}} ({{tr:ṣād}}) is not only a closing element here; it also appears as an independent surah-opening sign in 38:1.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah row gives the concrete 38:1 comparison, and the local surface ends with {{ar:ص}} ({{tr:ṣād}}), so the echo is valid without making Surah 38 control the local parse.

topics.headline: the cipher opens into mercy-mention
topics.reader_payoff: The reader follows the movement from unexplained recited sign in 19:1 into {{ar:ذِكْرُ رَحْمَتِ رَبِّكَ}} ({{tr:dhikru raḥmati rabbika}}) in 19:2, before the narrative begins.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows explicitly connect the 19:1 opener with the dhikr and mercy phrase in 19:2, so the bridge survives as a structural payoff rather than a new invented topic.

topics.headline: rarity, sound, variants, and position converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that no single mechanism carries the opener alone; uniqueness, articulation, qirāʾāt pressure, and threshold position stack on one surface.
topics.reason: The synthesis row summarizes features already retained under local guardrails: corpus uniqueness, broad sound path, qirāʾāt-sensitive form, and surah-opening placement.

review_notes: All CRITICAL rows are retained as used or narrowed because the guardrail evidence gives no contradiction; speculative initial/acrostic and variant-specific claims are narrowed so they do not replace the canonical rootless opener.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The ayah consists only of كٓهيعٓصٓ, five isolated letter forms with no rooted morphemes in the packet.
baseline_models.mechanism: Rootlessness blocks lexical and root-derived semantics, while the segmented form interrupts ordinary sentence processing and foregrounds the units from which discourse is made.

changed_reading.before: An unreadable or semantically empty opener.
changed_reading.after: A deliberate formal threshold that suspends lexical reading and presents articulated units before discourse, without yet decoding them.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate move into remembrance/mention recasts the rootless sequence as an arresting oral-memory cue: its value can lie in prompting and voicing recollection rather than carrying lexical content.

activation_trace.role: Recall after absence supplies the mnemonic recovery function assigned to the opener.
Mention moving on the tongue supplies the opener's oral and recited channel.

structural_cues: 19:2 follows the rootless opener immediately and begins with a nominal framing of the ensuing account as remembrance or mention.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency plus mnemonic and vocal branch images; I infer that the opener primes recollection through utterance. A live alternative is that it is only a formal boundary unrelated to the following act of remembrance.

changed_reading.after: A compact vocal mnemonic that arrests attention and primes the remembrance narrated next.

context_deltas.mechanism: A sequence that can be sounded but not lexically parsed becomes an acoustic veil: articulation is exposed while propositional content remains hidden, matching the nearby pattern of an audible yet private call.

activation_trace.role: Raised calling supplies the audible address against which the opener's sounded form can be heard.
Concealment supplies the withheld semantic side of the articulated sequence.
Calling through speech links the private prayer sequence to the opener's vocal form.

structural_cues: 19:3 repeats the call as verb and verbal noun, then qualifies it as hidden; 19:4 continues the first-person address to the Lord.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies calling, concealment, and prayer; I infer a formal analogy between hidden address and sound without lexical disclosure. The alternative is that hiddenness characterizes only Zechariah's prayer and does not retrospectively shape 19:1.

changed_reading.before: A mnemonic vocal cue with unresolved semantics.
changed_reading.after: A compressed mode of address whose sound is available while its propositional content stays veiled.

context_deltas.mechanism: Because the opener is encountered as a chain of letter-names rather than as one lexical word, the later concentration on a child's unprecedented name activates it as a prelude of naming and marking: identifiable units precede a uniquely identified person.

activation_trace.role: Naming as designation makes letter-names, rather than word meaning, the operative formal unit.
A visible identifying mark supplies the graphic counterpart to the spoken letter-names.

structural_cues: 19:7 realizes the same root at both the child's name and the denial of any prior namesake; 19:1 is composed of conventionally nameable letters but supplies no lexical designation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated naming, uniqueness, and a mapped branch of visible marking; I infer that the formal unit of 19:1 is the name/mark of each letter. The alternative is that the naming language has no retrospective relation to the opener.

changed_reading.before: Opaque units whose only evident force is interruption or sound.
changed_reading.after: A sequence of names and marks whose identifiability exceeds its propositional decodability, preparing the account of unprecedented naming.

context_deltas.mechanism: The requested sign is paired with suspended interpersonal speech, followed by communication through gesture-like revelation and then the book. This progression recasts the letter-only opener as a liminal sign-channel between voice and inscription: communicative, but not an ordinary sentence.

activation_trace.role: A manifest sign supplies communicative force without requiring sentential wording.
Intelligible speech connecting speakers is the channel explicitly suspended, defining the opener's contrastive mode.
Gesture supplies a replacement channel by which meaning passes without ordinary speech.
Inscription supplies the visible-sign analogue for the opener's glyph sequence.
Ordered letters and written text anchor the non-sentential opener to the later book-channel.

structural_cues: 19:10 negates speaking to people as the sign, 19:11 nevertheless transmits an instruction to the group, and 19:12 immediately foregrounds the book.
The focus ayah contains visible and pronounceable letter units but no rooted word or proposition.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies sign, speech suspension, nonverbal transmission, and ordered writing; I infer that 19:1 formally enacts meaningful signaling outside normal sentence speech. It may instead remain an opaque opener with no narrative enactment.

changed_reading.before: A rootless sequence that interrupts normal discourse.
changed_reading.after: A threshold sign poised between vocalization and inscription, communicating by marked units while withholding ordinary sentence speech.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: Projecting birth, creation, and reanimation onto textual composition is cross-domain and does not decode the letters. It remains anchored in the opener's isolated pre-word units and in the packet's explicit branch for ordering letters; render it only as a formal analogy by which dormant-looking units become discourse.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The opener presents isolated letters before any word, allowing joining and activation to map to its compositional form without assigning it a fabricated root.

activation_trace.role: Interrupted offspring supplies the sterile-seeming starting condition of the analogy.
Bringing creation into existence supplies emergence beyond the prior condition.
Knowable thinghood supplies the boundary crossed when bare units become an intelligible textual object.
Joining unit to unit supplies the compositional arrow from isolated letters toward discourse.
Ordering letters makes the emergence specifically textual rather than merely biological.
Stirring what is still from repose supplies the reactivation endpoint of the analogy.

changed_reading.before: A static preface of disconnected signs.
changed_reading.after: A dormant textual seed whose isolated units are joined and activated into discourse, analogically echoing impossible generation and renewed life.

strongest_changes: The sign-speech-gesture-book sequence makes the opener legible as communication outside ordinary sentence speech.
The repeated naming language makes letter-names and visible marks a distinct formal reading of the sequence.
Immediate remembrance and the hidden call preserve oral-mnemonic and veiled-address readings alongside the graphic one.
summary.what_was_special: Because 19:1 is rootless, the productive evidence was formal rather than lexical: segmentation, pronounceability, visible marking, and adjacency could be activated without inventing a root or choosing a single decoding.
remaining_uncertainties: No packet evidence determines a lexical expansion or referent for the five letters.
The mnemonic, concealed-call, naming, and sign-channel models may describe complementary functions or independent contextual projections.
The textual-germination model is deliberately contained as analogy because its causal direction is reader-supplied.

channel_generated_outputs.usage: External source manifest only. These generated outputs may inform channel-family/path context when the agent has file access, but first-pass review limits still apply: no established channel name, accept/reject claim, or maturity claim unless a future adjudicated ledger is present.

word_morpheme_spans.note: Accepted bridge links preserve independent analysis identities. Several analysis entries may share canonical morphemes. Read their distinct semantic claims; shared morphology alone is not duplication. Legacy aligned_qac_word_ref values are source observations, not QAC joins. Excluded source entries remain available with their explicit qualification.

word_analysis_qac_alignment.note: Legacy analysis and QAC numbers are separate source namespaces. Use accepted word_morpheme_spans for actual many-to-many joins. The legacy numbering observation is preserved, not used for alignment.

channel_review.note: first-pass blind review by a single reader; no adjudication, no accept/reject, no per-ayah channel maturity. Not a channel ledger.

channel_generated_outputs.note: Generated network-v3 channel discovery/family/path outputs are available as external quran-data files; read them only when channel detail is necessary, and do not treat them as an adjudicated channel ledger.

occurrence_evidence_trim.note: TRIMMED, NOT ABSENT. dictionary_entry.occurrence_evidence.occurrences and .ayahs are removed from every root by design: they are a per-occurrence QAC concordance and character-span alignment table carrying zero readings, branches or senses, and they dominated bundle size (~1.5 MB for a single common root). occurrence_evidence.summary (corpus frequency) and .forms (inflectional inventory) are retained. Dictionary/gloss branches are kept in full for every included Furuq root target.

branch_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.
